questions.q: What does explain() do when attached to a MongoDB query?
options: Returns the query's execution plan (and optionally real execution statistics) instead of, or in addition to, the query's data
Automatically creates any missing indexes the query needs
Deletes the query results and returns only an error log
Converts the query into a SQL statement for comparison
questions.explain: explain() shows what the query planner decided to do, from the winning plan to real execution statistics, depending on the mode.

questions.q: What is the default explain() mode, and what does it show?
options: queryPlanner — shows the winning plan without actually executing the query
executionStats — always runs the query and returns full timing data
allPlansExecution — always the default, showing every rejected plan
There is no default mode; a mode must always be specified
questions.explain: queryPlanner is the default mode and shows the chosen plan without running the query for real data.

questions.q: What does a winning plan stage of COLLSCAN indicate?
options: A full collection scan occurred — no usable index existed, equivalent to a SQL Server table scan
The query used an index efficiently
The collection has no documents in it
The query failed due to a syntax error
questions.explain: COLLSCAN means MongoDB scanned every document in the collection, the same red flag as a table scan in a SQL Server execution plan.

questions.q: In executionStats output, what does a large gap between totalDocsExamined and nReturned suggest?
options: The index being used isn't selective enough for this query, or the wrong index is being used
The query is guaranteed to be fast regardless of that gap
The collection needs to be dropped and recreated
This combination is impossible if an index was used at all
questions.explain: Examining far more documents than were actually returned signals an inefficient index for that particular query — the same red flag as a scan-heavy SQL Server plan.

questions.q: What does the IXSCAN stage in a winning plan mean?
options: An index was used to reach the relevant documents, roughly equivalent to a SQL Server index seek/scan
The query scanned the entire collection
The index was found to be corrupted
IXSCAN only appears when using the allPlansExecution mode
questions.explain: IXSCAN indicates MongoDB used an index rather than reading every document — the healthy outcome, comparable to an index seek in SQL Server.
